Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Child Labour Suggested Vocabulary work, duty, abuse, pain, overwork, mistreat, i
Topic 14.1: Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Child Labour Suggested Vocabulary work, duty, abuse, pain, overwork, mistreat, i in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we listen attentively when somebody is talking to us?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn-as learner responds to instructions appropriately.

Digital literacy-as learner interacts with digital devices when listening to audio and video recording

Values:
Unity as learners work in groups and in pairs.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship (social cohesion)- as learner work in groups in dialogues and language games

Link to other Learning Areas:

Attentive listening is significant in all the learning areas in the school curriculum.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
